title: refactor(tsconfig): rename tsconfig.base.json to tsconfig.tier-base.json
body:
Part of #9330. Executes the binding ruling recorded in comment 5651818643 (director seat, class-one self-adjudication, 2026-09-13): disposition (c) with the annotation — rename, update the extenders, put the measured `extends` graph in a JSONC header on both root configs, and **move no compiler option**.

⛔ **No compiler option moved, no gate added, nothing changes what any project compiles.** #7212's population question stays where it is.

## Chosen name: `tsconfig.tier-base.json`

The ruling delegated the pick ("you pick one consistent with the tier files it serves") and offered `tsconfig.tooling-base.json` as an example. `tier-base` is the one that survives measurement:

- The files that extend it are `tsconfig.node.json` and `tsconfig.react.json` — the repo-root **tier** configs, spelled `tsconfig.TIER.json`. `tsconfig.tier-base.json` is the name that series already implies.
- "tooling" would be false for the third extender, `examples/byo-backend-console/tsconfig.json`, which is an example app, not tooling.
- "package build base" would be false for all of them — no package extends this file, which is the whole point of the card.

## The measured `extends` graph

Re-derived from scratch on this branch's base `cb725e78f`, over **every one of the 94 tracked `tsconfig*.json` files in the repo**, read with **TypeScript's own JSONC reader** (`ts.readConfigFile` — the same parser `tsc` uses; these files are JSONC and a strict `JSON.parse` would throw).

| population | count | extends |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/*/tsconfig.json` | 40 | **38** → root `tsconfig.json`; 2 → nothing |
| `packages/*/tsconfig.test.json` | 37 | 36 → root `tsconfig.json`; 1 → its own sibling |
| all tracked `tsconfig*.json` | 94 | 75 → root `tsconfig.json`; **3** → the tier base; 13 → nothing; 3 → a sibling |

- The tier base is extended by exactly **3** files: `tsconfig.node.json`, `tsconfig.react.json`, `examples/byo-backend-console/tsconfig.json`.
- `packages/runner/tsconfig.json` and `packages/vscode-extension/tsconfig.json` extend **nothing** — recorded in both headers per the ruling, ⛔ not changed.
- Nothing under `apps/` or `examples/` extends the root `tsconfig.json`.

**Reader agreement with `tsc`, proven two-sided in one run** — `tsc --showConfig -p tsconfig.node.json` resolves `noImplicitReturns` / `declarationMap` / `sourceMap` / `esModuleInterop` / `noUnusedLocals: true` (options that exist only in the base ⇒ the `extends` my reader reported was really followed), and `tsc --showConfig -p tsconfig.scripts.json` resolves **none** of them (⇒ my reader's "extends nothing" is right too). A control that can fail in the direction that matters.

## ⚠️ Two corrections the ruling could not have known

**1. It names FOUR extenders; there are three.** `tsconfig.scripts.json` does **not** extend this file and must not start. Its own header argues the case at length: this file's `exclude` lists the test globs, so inheriting it would compile **none** of the `scripts/__tests__/` pin tests that project exists for — passing vacuously, the exact failure `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs` section 5b was written to catch. Its reference is prose only, so only the name was updated. Both new headers say so in as many words, so the next reader does not "complete" the ruling.

**2. The card says 30, the ruling says 38 — and 30 was never right.** Same population (`packages/*/tsconfig.json`), so the natural hypothesis is that they were measured at different commits. Re-measuring at the card's **own** stated commit `c64975e9f` settles it: 40 such files, **38** extending the root config — there as well as on this base (that probe re-ran on `cb725e78f` as a same-run control and returned 38 too). 30 matches no population in this repo at either commit: not the 38 non-private packages, not the 39 with a build script, not the 13 whose build invokes `tsc`, not the 40 with a `type-check` script. It is a miscount, not a narrower reading. The headers carry 38 and say why.

## The other half of a rename: everything that named the file by string

Swept all tracked text for the old basename **before** editing — 18 hits in 15 files, all of them printed in the report. Two are load-bearing beyond the `extends` edges:

- **`turbo.json`** lists `$TURBO_ROOT$/tsconfig.base.json` in the `inputs` of **two** tasks (`build`, `type-check`). Leaving it stale does not merely read wrong — it un-hashes a compiler-options file and the turbo-inputs pin tests go red in three directions at once.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** names it in the site-build path filter, which decides whether the docs build runs at all. Stale there fails **silently**.

Plus nine prose sites: `tsconfig.node.json`, `tsconfig.scripts.json`, four `scripts/__tests__/` docblocks, `scripts/check-skill-examples.mjs`, and four pending changesets.

### ⭐ Six of those prose sites were the card's own defect, in the wild

Six references did not merely name the file — they credited it with an option that governs **packages**, which never load it. Renaming them would have carried the error forward into a name that makes it *more* wrong. They are corrected to name the config that really carries the option, each measured first:

- `scripts/__tests__/one-authority-per-exported-name-6273.test.ts` — "`tsconfig.base.json` sets `isolatedModules: true` repo-wide". The option is real and repo-wide; it comes from the **root** `tsconfig.json`. (`tsc --showConfig -p packages/core/tsconfig.json` → `isolatedModules: true` present.)
- `scripts/check-skill-examples.mjs` — "mapping `@object-ui/*` to `src/` through `tsconfig.base.json`". The `paths` map to `src/` is the **root** config's; the tier base has no `paths` key at all. The sentence's own next clause already says "the root config", so it was self-contradictory.
- Four pending changesets crediting `removeComments: false` to it "deliberately". Measured: `@object-ui/core`'s resolved config sets `removeComments` **nowhere** (and inherits none of `declarationMap` / `sourceMap` / `noImplicitReturns`, while `tsconfig.node.json` inherits all three — the hitting control). The emitted comments and every byte count in those changesets are correct; only the attribution was wrong, and it now states what was measured. **Frontmatter untouched** — no bump level changed. `check:changeset-claims` is the gate that asks for exactly this re-read, and it is report-only by design.

`check:changeset-claims` flagged one further paragraph for re-reading: `.changeset/6349-types-internal-name-collisions-batch-1.md` names `one-authority-per-exported-name-6273.test.ts` and claims its `KNOWN_COLLISIONS` baseline is shrink-only, "43 entries → 40". My diff to that file is a **docblock hunk and nothing else**, touching no `KNOWN_COLLISIONS` entry — the claim is unaffected and stands.

## Verification

**Rename measured two-sided, with a hitting control and a nonsense control**, matched lines printed on both sides:

- old basename in tracked text: **18 hits / 15 files** on `cb725e78f` → **2** after, both the deliberate "renamed from" note in the two new headers. No `extends`, no path, no glob, nothing dangling.
- hitting control, same sweep, same run: the new basename returns **14 hits / 10 files** — non-empty, so the sweep can find a reference.
- nonsense control (`tsconfig.zzznotarealtier`): 0 hits, exit 1.
- the file itself: old path tracked 1 → 0, new path 0 → 1, old path absent on disk; `tsconfig.react.json` as a must-exist-both-sides control.

**Negative control on the edges** — pointing one extender back at the old name makes `tsc` fail loudly (`error TS5083: Cannot read file '.../tsconfig.base.json'`, exit 1), then restored byte-identical. All three extenders resolve their base afterwards (3/3 base-only options inherited, via `tsc --showConfig`).

**Ablation on the half that breaks silently** — with the fix committed, `turbo.json` was mutated back to the old name (mutation proven on disk by occurrence counts **and** a changed `git hash-object`, not by the editor's exit code). The two turbo-inputs pin tests went **red, 6 failures**, naming the fix in all three directions: coverage missing for `tsconfig.tier-base.json`, the old glob "matches no file in the repo", and the old entry "not required by any package's program any more". Restored with `git checkout HEAD -- turbo.json`, verified by hash equality against the HEAD blob and an empty `git diff HEAD` (not by an exit code), then re-run green.

**Gates, exit codes captured by redirect-then-capture, never across a pipe:**

| gate | PRE | POST |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | 0 | 0 |
| turbo-build-inputs + turbo-type-check-inputs + scripts-type-check + vitest-config-alias-targets pins | 0 (394 tests) | 0 (405 tests, +one-authority) |
| `pnpm check:changeset-claims` | 0 | 0 (report-only; 1 paragraph flagged, read, unaffected) |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 | 0 — "no changeset is owed" (18 files changed, 0 published source of a released package) |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | 0 | 0 (7587 tracked text files) |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | — | 0 (0 new citations) |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/` (the whole gate-pin suite) | — | 0 — 152 files, **4539 passed**, 2 skipped |
| `pnpm exec turbo run type-check --concurrency=2` (whole workspace) | — | 0 — **81/81 tasks**, 5m40s |
| `pnpm exec turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/example-byo-backend-console` (the one package whose config chain changed, through a real 31-task build closure) | — | 0 |
| `pnpm type-check:e2e` / `:vitest-setup` / `:vitest-config` / `:coverage` | — | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| real compile through the now-commented root config (`tsc --noEmit -p packages/types/tsconfig.json`) | — | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` | — | NOT GOVERNED, 18 paths, 0 matched |

Both new headers use `//` line comments, not `/* */`, for the reason `tsconfig.scripts.json` records: a glob containing `**` followed by `/` closes a block comment early, and a tsconfig that silently fails to parse falls back to including the entire repository. `tsc --showConfig -p tsconfig.json` still parses with the header and still resolves the full `paths` table.

**No changeset:** `check-changeset-presence` reports none owed — no published source of a released package changed. `examples/byo-backend-console` is private.

⛔ Draft on purpose. The PM lands it.
